newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sees OECD membership ratified by December.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sees OECD membership ratified by December.

text.p: The South Korean government expects parliament to ratify the country's entry into the Paris-based OECD club of rich nations by December, a senior finance ministry official said on Thursday.

"We should get it passed by the end of the current session," said Cho Yoon-je, senior counsellor to the Finance Minister. The current session of the National Assembly is scheduled to end on December 18.

Opposition parties have threatened to block South Korea's entry into the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) by opposing ratification in parliament, where President Kim Young-sam's ruling party has a slim majority.
Cho, however, said the opposition "did not have a concrete case" and said the government was well prepared to answer their concerns.
Critics and opposition parties warn against the adverse impact of further prying open local markets to offshore competition, especially on small and medium-sized industries.

They also fear OECD membership will only hamper the economy by triggering a rush speculative funds into local markets as investors focus on South Korea's relatively high interest rates, now hovering around 12 percent.
Cho attempted to allay those fears on Wednesday, telling foreign journalists the country would adhere to a strict timetable for opening its markets to ensure stability.

South Korea, which was invited to join the OECD last Friday, would be the second Asian nation after Japan to enter the 28-member club. From the wider Asia-Pacific area, Australia and New Zealand are also members of the OECD.
